title: Turbidity gave no clear heat buffer for annual coral cover change in four Atlantic and Pacific samples in 1998-2019
abstract: We tested whether site mean turbidity changed the link between survey-date heat and annual hard-coral cover change. HeatCRD version 1 gave 1,110 matched annual pairs at 425 sites. We matched site, source, month and depth. Four ocean and period models controlled first-survey heat, its turbidity interaction, initial cover, depth, year, month and source. The second-heat slope changed by -3.69, +1.82, +4.99 and +0.89 cover points per four TSA degree-heating weeks per turbidity doubling. All four corrected intervals included zero. Only 66 pairs had second-survey heat of at least four; 14 had that heat and moderate turbidity. Country clusters, initial-cover removal, a turbidity limit and a linear turbidity scale did not establish a common buffer. These selected records do not show that turbidity has no effect. Sparse heat support, site mean optics, survey-date heat, source imbalance and missing visits limit inference. The package gives source hashes, matched data, model matrices, code and independent checks.

display.caption: Left: turbidity interaction estimates with four-test corrected intervals. Positive values agree with a cover-loss buffer. Right: high-heat support by turbidity class. Optical attenuation is a site mean, not a survey-date measurement.

citations.reason: Its annual matching design informs this new interaction test. The raw source and many observations overlap. No independent data validation is claimed.
Prior turbidity interaction study uses bleaching. We test annual cover change with another archive, with overlapping source programs.
